chunks: I am commanded to worship the Lord of this land, He who blessed it; and to Him belongs all things; and I am commanded to be one of those who submit.
ai.seo_question: What is the Lord of this land commanded to do in Surah An-Naml?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet's (SAWW) specific mission to Mecca, linking the sanctity of the city (Haram) directly to the sovereignty of Allah, who is the owner of all things. It reinforces the concept of Tawhid by commanding submission not just in ritual, but as a comprehensive state of being among the Muslims, reflecting the unique spiritual status of the Prophet in the holy sanctuary.
